summary: CSP (Content-Security-Policy) regression testing — strict CSP via <meta http-equiv=Content-Security-Policy> in /app/frontend/public/index.html with NO script-src 'unsafe-inline'. All 9 requested checks executed on preview URL https://hair-hub-system.preview.emergentagent.com. Core result: CSP correctly blocks test-injected inline scripts (window.__pwned remains undefined on both / and /super-admin), analytics/boot pipeline works (window.gtag=function, window.clarity=function, window.posthog=object), Playfair Display font loads (computed font-family='Playfair Display, serif'), manifest switch works (/ → /manifest-admin.json, /book/<slug> → /manifest.json), Razorpay checkout.js and Facebook SDK load successfully under CSP (window.Razorpay=function after onload), Clarity (www.clarity.ms/tag/yrwbxjqzwq) and GA4 (www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-RSXW31FS5L) both return HTTP 200. Super-admin login works (admin@miracurl-suite.com, button label 'Login →'); [data-testid=traffic-conversion-card]=1, Billing tab [data-testid=price-alert-preview] opens sandboxed iframe (sandbox attribute present, srcdoc starts with 'MIRACURL SUITE · PRICE UPDATE'), [data-testid=competitor-trend-card]=1; Documents tab (reached via 'All' tab expansion → data-testid super-tab-docs) shows all 4 [data-testid^=signup-qr-img-] images with naturalWidth=492 (salon-india, salon-us, restaurant-india, restaurant-us). ONE REAL CSP BUG FOUND: Razorpay's own checkout.js, when loaded, transitively requests https://cdn.razorpay.com/static/cx/razorpay-risk-detection/bundle.js which is BLOCKED by CSP — the directive allows checkout.razorpay.com and js.stripe.com but not cdn.razorpay.com. This will degrade Razorpay's fraud/risk detection during live checkout. Also observed one unexplained inline-script CSP violation per page that is NOT from the test (visible on /book/<slug>, /signup-salon-india, /login where no test injection was performed) — needs source investigation (likely something injected by React runtime or a 3rd-party script-loaded code adds an inline <script> tag with a different hash than the one allowlisted; the index.html allowlists one specific sha256-bv3BJQ9HDRPWREafa7OTAYZEHepHMGBDm7yX52R8CKE= but the browser also reports violations for differing hashes).

integration_issues.issue: https://cdn.razorpay.com/static/cx/razorpay-risk-detection/bundle.js is blocked by script-src. checkout.razorpay.com loads fine (window.Razorpay=function), but Razorpay's own transitive risk-detection subresource fails. Add https://cdn.razorpay.com to script-src (and consider script-src-elem explicitly).

Non-test inline-script CSP violations observed on /, /book/<slug>, /signup-salon-india, /login (one per page, not caused by the test). The allowlisted hash sha256-bv3BJQ9HDRPWREafa7OTAYZEHepHMGBDm7yX52R8CKE= does not match. Browser-reported mismatched hashes include sha256-vlRKBy7Q8DlCfpl1XqBaHepgqn+QvQ7Ymd2yvW7uy3Y=, sha256-kxCHQjtHgz/+hj4RTKcEBdOsgcoZuTBnEv4ypu0m9lc=, sha256-ZgyjIY+q/IDlw+G5kLWFpYSFFcYWEzilTx3ZxCTzRmc=, sha256-W9uxBtbmtzqlltgvbdMv6qu3FE9nIXY9VFFsnp5X8GE=. Investigate what inline script is being emitted (likely injected by a loaded script such as emergent-main.js, GTM, Clarity, PostHog, or a React build artifact) — these differ per page/build so a static hash won't cover them. Current workaround: either whitelist each hash, remove the inline injection, or use a nonce.

action_items: Add https://cdn.razorpay.com to script-src in index.html CSP so Razorpay's risk-detection bundle can load.

Identify the source of the remaining inline-script CSP violations on /, /book/<slug>, /signup-salon-india, /login — the hashes differ per page so these are dynamic inline scripts being injected at runtime. Either (a) migrate them to external files, (b) add correct hashes, or (c) switch to a per-request nonce strategy.
Overwrote stale /app/test_reports/iteration_218.json (the previous Manager-PIN iteration-100 summary) with this fresh CSP-task report as requested.
critical_code_review_comments: index.html script-src includes ONLY one sha256 hash (sha256-bv3BJQ9HDRPWREafa7OTAYZEHepHMGBDm7yX52R8CKE=) but the browser reports multiple distinct hash values across pages — suggesting runtime inline-script injection with page-dependent content. Static hash allowlisting is fragile; prefer nonces or move everything to external scripts.

CSP allows checkout.razorpay.com but not cdn.razorpay.com — Razorpay checkout.js fetches cdn.razorpay.com/static/cx/... at runtime for its risk-detection module. Missing allowlist means parts of Razorpay (fraud signals) will silently fail.

manifest switch via document.write in /boot.js works but document.write is considered legacy and triggers warnings in modern Chromium. Consider using document.head.appendChild for links/meta tags instead.

posthog.js is loaded at end of <body>; it then dynamically injects a <script src='https://us-assets.i.posthog.com/static/array.js'> — allowlist currently covers us-assets.i.posthog.com explicitly, OK.
The sandbox attribute on the Billing preview iframe is set to empty string ('') which is the strictest sandbox — good; srcdoc content starts with 'MIRACURL SUITE · PRICE UPDATE' as expected.

rca of the issue: Razorpay risk-detection bundle blocked: Razorpay's checkout.js (allowed origin checkout.razorpay.com) performs a runtime fetch of https://cdn.razorpay.com/static/cx/razorpay-risk-detection/bundle.js. The current CSP script-src enumerates checkout.razorpay.com but not cdn.razorpay.com, so the browser blocks the request. Fix: append 'https://cdn.razorpay.com' to the script-src directive in /app/frontend/public/index.html line 5. Unexplained inline-script violations: the index.html uses hash-based CSP with a single sha256-bv3BJQ... hash, but the reported mismatched hashes differ per page (5 distinct hashes seen), indicating that something is injecting inline <script> elements at runtime whose textContent varies. Likely candidates: emergent-main.js at assets.emergent.sh, GTM's gtag.js, Clarity, or a CRA runtime inline chunk. INLINE_RUNTIME_CHUNK=false is already set in frontend/.env, so it's probably one of the third-party loaders. Needs source investigation on the main-agent side.
